- Model consistently underestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then gradually catches up or overshoots later.
- Overshoots occur after sharp price spikes (e.g., 38.18 → 42.10), with model peaking too early or too high.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to recent volatility, underestimating sustained upward trends.
- Lagged response: model reacts to recent history with delay, missing sudden reversals or new catalysts.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to be too conservative in the first half, then become more aggressive toward end of horizon.
- Avoid averaging recent highs; model often ignores or underweights recent peaks when forecasting future values.
- Correct for “overfitting to recent low” — model tends to assume prices will stay near recent lows, even when trend is upward.
